name: Skylar Alston
strengths: Alston (#11) triggers downhill with no hesitation — diagnoses run and attacks A/B gaps, often disrupting in the backfield before the ball clears the line.
Alston takes on pullers/climb blocks, uses hands to disengage, and anchors his gap instead of getting washed; scrape stays square while he flows to the numbers.
Alston finishes violently through the hips and stops momentum; also shows edge-rush bend/burst and active hands when aligned as a pressure LB.
weaknesses: Alston's highlight package is run/blitz heavy — deep zone drops, hip flips in coverage, and TE/RB matching need more sample for SEC third-down trust.
Alston occasionally plays high into lead blockers and wins with upper-body strength; pad level/leverage must tighten vs SEC climb blocks.
comparison: Alston comps to Ty'Ron Hopper — 6-2 physical MIKE mold; sudden downhill trigger, box control, and violent run fits over pure open-space track speed (size-matched within ~1–2"; not a Florida-alum default).
projection: Alston projects as Year 1 core special teams + rotational early-down run thumper, Year 2–3 compete/start at MIKE, with multi-year SEC box-anchor ceiling if coverage development catches his downhill instincts.
schemeFit: Alston fits White's odd front as a MIKE/downhill second-level piece who fills A/B, sheds climb blocks, and can pressure off the edge in package looks.
